title: Seventh Word Proof For Patience And Reliance Weakness As A Document

questions.question: What are the two medicines in this passage?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah with patience, and depending on Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: When a person feels weak, who should he depend on?
questions.answer: He should depend on Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say a trusting person remembers during a hard trouble?
questions.answer: He remembers that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: How can knowing Allah change the way a person feels about being weak?
questions.answer: It can make him feel peace and even sweetness instead of only sadness.

questions.question: What baby example is given to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: A baby feels safe by running to its mother when afraid.

questions.question: Is a mother’s mercy bigger than Allah’s mercy, or only a tiny part of it?
questions.answer: It is only a tiny part of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Why do wise people say they have no real power by themselves?
questions.answer: Because they know all true strength comes from Allah.

questions.question: What do wise people use to draw near to Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: Their weakness and their fear of Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage teach people to be proud of themselves, or to seek Allah’s help?
questions.answer: It teaches them to seek Allah’s help.

questions.question: What is one main lesson from this passage?
questions.answer: When people know they are weak and trust Allah, they find safety and comfort.

questions.question: What is the first medicine named in the passage?
questions.answer: Trust in Allah with patience.

questions.question: What is the second medicine named in the passage?
questions.answer: Relying on the Creator’s power and trusting His wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the passage say a person does not need to live in constant fear?
questions.answer: Because Allah is in control of everything.

questions.question: What should a believer do when a very hard problem happens?
questions.answer: He should turn to Allah and trust Him.

questions.question: What feeling can come from fearing Allah in the right way?
questions.answer: A good and comforting feeling can come from it.

questions.question: How does the story of the baby help us understand trusting Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that a weak one feels safe by taking refuge in the one who cares for him.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does the kindness of mothers really come from?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What have wise people chosen instead of trusting their own strength?
questions.answer: They choose to take refuge in Allah.

questions.question: Why do wise people admit they are powerless?
questions.answer: Because it helps them turn sincerely to Allah.

questions.question: If a person thinks he is strong all by himself, would that match the lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: No. The passage teaches that people should know their need for Allah.

questions.question: Which two actions are called medicines here?
questions.answer: Patience with trust in Allah, and confidence in Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: What mighty ability of Allah is mentioned to show His power?
questions.answer: He can make things happen by His command.

questions.question: In the worst hardship, what does the trusting person do first?
questions.answer: He gives himself over to Allah and depends on Him.

questions.question: What kind of Lord does the passage describe Allah as for the person who trusts Him?
questions.answer: A very caring and merciful Lord.

questions.question: Does the passage show weakness as always bad, or as something that can lead a person to Allah?
questions.answer: It shows weakness can lead a person to Allah.

questions.question: What does the baby want when it feels small and scared?
questions.answer: It wants safety in its mother’s care.

questions.question: Why is the baby example useful in this passage?
questions.answer: It helps explain how safety can come from turning to someone stronger and kinder.

questions.question: Compared with Allah’s mercy, how great is human mercy?
questions.answer: Human mercy is very small.

questions.question: What have wise people done with their fear of Allah?
questions.answer: They have used it to help themselves turn to Allah.

questions.question: What is the passage teaching about real strength?
questions.answer: Real strength is not in ourselves; it is in depending on Allah.

questions.question: In this passage, what helps heal the heart like medicine?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah, being patient, and believing in His power and wisdom.

questions.question: When someone knows he cannot do everything, what should he remember about Allah?
questions.answer: He should remember that Allah can do all things.

questions.question: What words does the passage mention a believer says in a disaster?
questions.answer: He says that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: When that child is afraid, where does he find comfort?
questions.answer: He finds comfort with his mother.

questions.question: What does this example teach us about Allah’s servants?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s servants should run to Him for safety.

questions.question: Are mothers’ kind hearts the highest mercy, or signs of Allah’s greater mercy?
questions.answer: They are signs of Allah’s greater mercy.

questions.question: Why do wise people stay away from bragging about their own power?
questions.answer: Because they know they truly need Allah.

questions.question: Finish the idea in a simple way: weakness plus trust in Allah brings what?
questions.answer: It brings peace and closeness to Allah.

questions.question: What two things are called medicines in the target passage?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah with patience, and relying on His power and wisdom.

questions.question: Who is the One a weak person should lean on?
questions.answer: Allah, the Creator.

questions.question: What should a believer do instead of panicking in a calamity?
questions.answer: He should trust Allah and return his heart to Him.

questions.question: Can fear of Allah ever be good for a person in this passage?
questions.answer: Yes. It can bring comfort and safety.

questions.question: How is a baby’s safety connected to the main idea?
questions.answer: The baby feels safe by going to caring protection, just as a believer turns to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the mercy of all mothers together?
questions.answer: It is only a small sign of divine mercy.

questions.question: What did wise people strongly say about their own strength?
questions.answer: They said they had no power by themselves.

questions.question: What did wise people choose as their helper before Allah?
questions.answer: Their helplessness and their fear of Him.

questions.question: What should we learn from the wise people in this passage?
questions.answer: We should be humble and seek help from Allah.

questions.question: What are the two cures taught in this passage?
questions.answer: Patience with trust in Allah, and confidence in Allah’s power and wise plan.

questions.question: Why can a person who trusts Allah be brave in trouble?
questions.answer: Because he knows Allah rules over everything.

questions.question: What truth does the believer remember when pain or loss comes?
questions.answer: That he belongs to Allah and will go back to Him.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can a person who knows Allah feel even in weakness?
questions.answer: He can feel a special peace and sweetness.

questions.question: What example from family life is used to explain this?
questions.answer: The example of a baby feeling safe with its mother.

questions.question: What does the baby know about itself in that example?
questions.answer: It knows it is helpless and needs care.

questions.question: How does the passage compare a mother’s mercy with Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: A mother’s mercy is only a tiny glimpse of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What did wise people do because they understood this?
questions.answer: They took refuge in Allah instead of trusting themselves.

questions.question: Did wise people treat weakness as shameful or as a way to ask Allah for help?
questions.answer: They treated it as a way to ask Allah for help.

questions.question: What is the big message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: When we know our need and trust Allah, our hearts become stronger and calmer.
